checks.rationale: Privileges follow the certificate, the category and the person's authorisation, and they differ between conventional certified aircraft and some recreational categories, and from state to state.

checks.question: The HKS 700T turns at 5,300 rpm and its reduction gearbox has a ratio of 2.13 to 1. How fast does the propeller turn, to the nearest 10 rpm?
checks.hint: Divide the engine speed by the reduction ratio.
checks.rationale: 5,300 ÷ 2.13 = 2,488 rpm, about 2,490. The engine makes its power at a high speed and the gearbox slows the propeller to a speed at which it is efficient.

checks.question: Why does a small engine that makes its power at about 5,000 rpm drive its propeller through a reduction gearbox?
checks.hint: Think about the propeller blade tips.
answers: The propeller would lose efficiency as its tips approached the speed of sound, so it has to turn slower than the engine
The gearbox makes the engine run faster
A propeller cannot be fitted to a direct-drive engine
The gearbox cools the engine
checks.rationale: Whenever the blade tips approach the speed of sound the efficiency of a propeller decreases rapidly. A reduction gearbox lets the engine turn fast, for power from a small, light engine, while the propeller turns slowly enough.

checks.question: Match each engine to how it drives its propeller.
checks.hint: Think about which engines turn fastest.

pairs.right: Directly, at 3,300 rpm
Through a reduction gearbox of 2.13 to 1
Directly, at 2,750 rpm
Through a reduction gear of 0.667 to 1

checks.rationale: The Jabiru and the O-200 are direct-drive. The HKS 700T runs at about 5,300 rpm and uses a 2.13:1 reduction. The GTSIO-520-H runs near 3,400 rpm and uses a 0.667:1 reduction gear.

checks.question: Tap the piston.
checks.hint: It slides up and down inside the cylinder barrel.
checks.rationale: The piston takes the pressure of combustion and passes it, through the pin and the connecting rod, to the crankshaft. The rings sit in grooves round it and the piston pin runs across it.

checks.question: Tap a piston ring.
checks.hint: The rings sit in grooves round the piston, above the pin.
checks.rationale: This piston has four rings: two compression rings above and two oil-control rings below. Any of the four is right.

checks.question: Tap the connecting rod.
checks.hint: It joins the piston to the crankshaft.
checks.rationale: The connecting rod has an I-beam shank, a small end at the piston pin and a big end that is split into a body and a cap round the crankpin. Either the body or the cap is the rod.

checks.question: Tap the crankshaft throw.
checks.hint: It is the offset part that the big end of the rod wraps round.
checks.rationale: The throw is the offset part of the crankshaft, with the crankpin the big end of the connecting rod turns on. The model shows one throw of the crankshaft.

checks.question: Tap the intake valve.
checks.hint: It lets the fresh charge into the cylinder. There are two valves in the head.
checks.rationale: The intake valve admits the fresh charge from the induction system. On a real engine you can tell it from the exhaust valve by the pipework connected to its port.

checks.question: Tap the exhaust valve.
checks.hint: It lets the burned gas out of the cylinder.
checks.rationale: The exhaust valve opens to let the burned gas out to the exhaust stack. It passes the hot gas, so it runs hotter than the intake valve.

checks.question: Tap a spark plug.
checks.hint: It screws into the cylinder head and ignites the mixture.
checks.rationale: Each cylinder has two spark plugs, an upper and a lower, fed by the two magnetos. Any part of either plug is right here.

checks.question: Tap a magneto.
checks.hint: It supplies the ignition energy. There are two of them.
checks.rationale: The engine has two magnetos, which are driven by the gear train and supply the ignition energy to the two spark plugs in each cylinder. Either is right.

checks.question: Tap the engine-driven fuel pump.
checks.hint: It delivers fuel to the engine. In this model it is driven through the camshaft gear cluster.
checks.rationale: The engine-driven fuel pump delivers fuel to the induction system. It is fitted on the accessory case and, in this model, driven through the camshaft gear cluster; the later -H installation differs from the older one.

checks.question: Tap the alternator.
checks.hint: It generates the aircraft's electrical power.
checks.rationale: The alternator generates electrical power. In this teaching model it stands on a display fixture at the front, with the transfer from the engine omitted.

checks.question: Match each external part to the system it belongs to.
checks.hint: Think about what each system does for the engine.

pairs.right: Ignition
Cooling
Lubrication
Fuel and induction
Exhaust

checks.rationale: The magneto supplies the spark, the fins carry heat from the cylinder to the air, the oil filter cleans the oil, the carburettor or servo meters the fuel into the induction air, and the stack collects the burned gas.

checks.question: Match each defect term to its meaning.
checks.hint: These are the handbook's definitions.

pairs.right: Loss of metal by chemical or electrochemical action
Wear from two parts rubbing together under light pressure
A partial separation of the material, from vibration, overloading, stress or fatigue
A small rounded depression where the part was struck

checks.rationale: Use the inspector's words in your notes. Corrosion products are easily removed by mechanical means, a crack may be a few thousandths deep or run through the full thickness, and a dent is rounded where a nick has sharp sides.

checks.question: Which action is part of the FAA warning before you move a propeller by hand?
checks.hint: Think about what could make the engine fire.
answers: Disconnect all spark plug leads
Set the mixture control to full rich
Leave the magneto switches on BOTH so the engine is ready
checks.rationale: The warning lists disconnecting all spark plug leads, magneto switches off and P-leads grounded, throttle closed, mixture at idle cut-off, brakes set and wheels blocked, tie-downs fitted, and never standing in the arc of the blades.

checks.question: You see a flat gray or sooty black streak on an exhaust pipe next to a clamp. What does it most likely show?
checks.hint: Hot gas that escapes leaves a trace.
answers: An exhaust gas leak at that joint
Normal staining that needs no action
Oil leaking from the sump
checks.rationale: The handbook says an exhaust leak is indicated by a flat gray or sooty black streak on the pipes in the area of the leak, usually from poor alignment of two mated parts. The clamps are loosened and the parts repositioned for a gas-tight fit.

checks.question: What is the primary purpose of the firewall?
checks.hint: It is the foremost bulkhead of the engine compartment, made of fire-resistant material.
answers: To confine any engine fire to the engine nacelle
To carry the weight of the engine
To cool the cylinders
checks.rationale: Without the firewall an engine fire would have ready access to the inside of the aircraft. It is also a mounting surface for units and the point where lines, linkages and wiring between engine and aircraft are disconnected.

checks.question: At the end of the compression stroke, where is the piston?
checks.hint: Compression squeezes the charge into the smallest space.
answers: At top dead centre
At bottom dead centre
Halfway down the cylinder
Moving fastest, at the middle of its travel
checks.rationale: Compression pushes the piston up to the top of its travel, where the charge is in its smallest volume and ignition is about to start the power stroke.

checks.question: How many degrees of crankshaft rotation does one complete four-stroke cycle take?
checks.hint: Two complete turns of the crankshaft.
checks.rationale: The four strokes need two complete revolutions of the crankshaft, 2 × 360 = 720 degrees, so each cylinder fires once in every two revolutions.

checks.question: The crankshaft turns 1,200 times. How many times does the camshaft turn in that time?
checks.hint: The camshaft turns at half the crankshaft speed.
checks.rationale: The camshaft always turns at half the crankshaft speed, so 1,200 turns of the crankshaft are 600 turns of the camshaft. Each valve opens once in every two crankshaft turns.

checks.question: On an opposed engine, how do the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear compare?
checks.hint: The camshaft turns slower, so its gear is larger.
answers: The camshaft gear has twice as many teeth, so the camshaft turns at half speed
The camshaft gear has half as many teeth, so the camshaft turns at half speed
The two gears are the same size, so both turn at the same speed
The camshaft gear has twice as many teeth, so the camshaft turns at twice the speed
checks.rationale: The cam gear is twice the size of the crankshaft gear and turns at half its speed, because each valve opens only once in the two turns of a cycle.

checks.question: Match each term to its meaning.
checks.hint: Think about what happens near TDC.

pairs.right: The intake valve opens before TDC
The exhaust valve closes after TDC
Both valves are off their seats at the same time
The distance the piston travels from TDC to BDC

checks.rationale: Lead is early opening, lag is late closing, and overlap is the short time near TDC when both are open. The stroke is the piston travel between the two dead centres.

checks.question: Put these parts in the order the force of combustion passes through them.
checks.hint: Start at the piston and end at the part that turns.
items: Piston
Piston pin
Connecting rod
Crankpin (throw)
Crankshaft
checks.rationale: The pressure acts on the piston, which pushes on the connecting rod through the piston pin. The rod pushes on the crankpin, which is off the centre line, and that turns the crankshaft.

checks.question: A four-cylinder, four-stroke engine fires one cylinder every how many degrees of crankshaft rotation?
checks.hint: Divide the 720 degrees of a cycle by the number of cylinders.
checks.rationale: 720 ÷ 4 = 180 degrees. Each power stroke lasts 180 degrees, so on a four-cylinder engine one power stroke follows the other without overlap.

checks.question: A crankshaft has six throws. Which engine does the handbook link it to?
checks.hint: The number of crankpins must match the cylinder arrangement.
answers: A six-cylinder opposed engine
A four-cylinder opposed engine
A single-row radial engine
A two-cylinder opposed engine
checks.rationale: The handbook says the six-throw shaft is used on six-cylinder inline engines, 12-cylinder V-type engines and six-cylinder opposed engines, and the four-throw shaft on four-cylinder opposed or inline engines. A single-row radial has a single throw.

checks.question: Match each part to the material the handbook gives for it.
checks.hint: Think about heat and strength.

pairs.right: Aluminium alloy, light and a good conductor of heat
Steel, with the cooling fins machined on it
Most often gray cast iron
Forged alloy steel with hardened (nitrided) surfaces
Cast aluminium alloy, sometimes magnesium

checks.rationale: The head is aluminium alloy for lightness and heat conduction, and the barrel is steel. Rings are most often gray cast iron. The crankshaft is forged from a strong alloy steel and nitrided for wear, and the crankcase is cast aluminium alloy or magnesium.

checks.question: Which valve is made of the more heat-resistant alloy, and why?
checks.hint: One valve passes the burned gas.
answers: The exhaust valve, because it runs hotter than the intake valve
The intake valve, because it runs hotter than the exhaust valve
Neither: both are made of the same alloy
The intake valve, because it is larger
checks.rationale: Intake valves run at lower temperatures than exhaust valves, so exhaust valves are made of more heat-resistant alloys such as nichrome, silchrome or cobalt-chromium steel.

checks.question: In the engine model GTSIO-520, what does the letter G stand for?
checks.hint: The prefixes describe features of the engine.
answers: A geared engine
A gasoline engine
A generator drive
A ground-running engine
checks.rationale: In the course text, G is the prefix for a geared engine. GTSIO-520 reads: geared, turbo-supercharged, fuel-injected, opposed, 520 cubic inches.

checks.question: Match each defect term to its meaning.
checks.hint: Think about the cause of each.

pairs.right: Surface damage from excessive heat
Deep scratches from foreign particles between moving parts
Small hollows, usually from corrosion
Severe chafing or fretting, with metal moved from one part to the other

checks.rationale: The handbook defines burning as damage from excessive heat, scoring as a series of deep scratches, pitting as small hollows of irregular shape, and galling as a severe condition of chafing or fretting with transfer of metal.

checks.question: A cylinder wall is scored and the piston rings can no longer seal against it. What would you expect to find?
checks.hint: Think about what the rings are for.
answers: Low compression, because gas leaks past the piston
High compression, because the rings grip harder
Better cooling, because oil reaches the wall
No effect on the engine
checks.rationale: The rings seal the gap between piston and cylinder wall. Leakage past the piston is a frequent cause of loss of compression, so a wall that rings cannot seal against shows up as low compression.

checks.question: Tap a pushrod.
checks.hint: It carries the lift from the tappet to the rocker arm.
checks.rationale: The pushrod is the tubular rod between the tappet and the rocker arm. It lies inside its housing and carries the lift from the cam to the rocker arm.

checks.question: Tap a valve spring.
checks.hint: It closes the valve and holds it on its seat.
checks.rationale: Each valve is closed by two or three helical springs, one inside the other. The springs close the valve and hold it on its seat.

checks.question: Put these steps for taking a cylinder off in the order the handbook gives them.
checks.hint: Pipes and covers first, the cylinder itself last.
items: Remove the intake and exhaust pipes and the rocker covers
Turn the crankshaft to TDC on the compression stroke and remove and mark the pushrods
Remove all the hold-down nuts except two opposite each other
Support the cylinder, remove the last two nuts and draw it off straight
Remove the piston from the connecting rod, then support the rod
checks.rationale: Openings are protected and the obstructions come off first. The pushrods come out with the piston at TDC on compression, when both rocker arms are free. The cylinder is held by two nuts until it is supported. Once the cylinder is off, the piston comes off the rod, and the rod must then be supported so it is not damaged.

checks.question: Why turn the crankshaft to TDC on the compression stroke before you remove the pushrods?
checks.hint: Think about the two rocker arms.
answers: It relieves the pressure on both the intake and the exhaust rocker arms
It puts the exhaust valve fully open
It locks the crankshaft so it cannot turn
It drains the oil from the cylinder
checks.rationale: With the piston at TDC on the compression stroke both valves are shut, so neither rocker arm is loaded by its valve spring and the pushrods can be taken out.

checks.question: When you fit a piston with its rings into a cylinder, what do you do with the ring gaps?
checks.hint: Gaps in line would give gas a straight path.
answers: Stagger them around the piston and check each ring is in its own groove
Line them up on the thrust side of the piston
Line them up with the piston pin
Leave them as they come out of the box
checks.rationale: The handbook says to stagger the ring gaps around the piston and to check that the rings are in the correct grooves and positioned correctly, because some are oil scrapers and others are pumper rings.

checks.question: Why are the body, socket and plunger of a hydraulic tappet kept together as a set?
checks.hint: Think about the leak-down rate.
answers: They are selectively fitted to give the specified leak-down rate
They are painted the same colour
They are always interchangeable
They must be cleaned in the same solvent
checks.rationale: The body, socket and plunger of each tappet are selectively fitted to obtain the specified leak-down rate, so parts from different tappets must not be mixed.

checks.question: In the quick test of a hydraulic tappet, the plunger kicks back promptly when it is tapped down. What does that show?
checks.hint: Trapped air is being compressed.
answers: Good compression: the tappet is acceptable if nothing else is wrong
The tappet must be discarded
The check valve is leaking badly
The oil holes are blocked
checks.rationale: A prompt kick-back, from the compression of trapped air, shows good compression. Rapid leakage would point to dirt on the check valve or seat or a worn plunger.

checks.question: The GTSIO-520 manual gives the outer valve spring, compressed to 1.275 inch, a serviceable limit of 118 pounds. A spring reads 109 pounds at that length. By how many pounds is it below the serviceable limit?
checks.hint: Subtract the reading from the limit.
checks.rationale: 118 − 109 = 9 pounds below the serviceable limit, so the spring fails the test. The limit is from the manual's table of limits (March 1981); for any engine, use the current data for that engine. The reading of 109 pounds is made up for practice.

checks.question: After you reposition a leaking exhaust joint and tighten the nuts to the specified torque, the joint is still loose. What do you do?
checks.hint: Think about what a stretched nut does.
answers: Replace the bolts and nuts, because they have probably stretched
Tighten them beyond the specified torque
Leave them, since the joint was repositioned
Fit a larger washer
checks.rationale: If tightening to the specified torque does not take up the looseness, the bolts and nuts should be replaced, since they have probably stretched. The torque must not be exceeded.

checks.question: What must you never use to mark exhaust parts?
checks.hint: The mark is absorbed by the hot metal.
answers: A lead pencil
A felt-tip pen
A paper tag
A tie-on label
checks.rationale: The lead from a pencil, like zinc from zinc-plated tools, is absorbed by the metal when it is heated. It softens the metal around the mark and leads to cracks.

checks.question: Put the four things Practical B asks of every part in order.
checks.hint: Start with what it is.
items: Identify the part
State its function
Describe how it is built
Recognise a sign that it is not in good condition
checks.rationale: The practical follows one pattern for each part: identify it, state its function, describe its construction, and recognise an abnormal condition, relating it to what the part does.

checks.question: Under the Tanzanian airworthiness regulations, which methods must a person doing maintenance use?
checks.hint: Think about whose data applies.
answers: Those in the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness, or others approved by the Authority
Whatever method the engineer remembers
Only the methods in the engineer's own notes
The cheapest method that completes the job
checks.rationale: Regulation 30 requires the methods, techniques and practices prescribed in the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or instructions for continued airworthiness, or methods the Authority approves where those documents are not available.

checks.question: Which item is on the Tanzanian regulation's list for the engine and nacelle group of an inspection?
checks.hint: It is a part that holds the engine to the airframe.
answers: The engine mount, for cracks and looseness of mounting
The seat belts, for poor condition
The tyres, for wear and cuts
The wing fabric, for deterioration
checks.rationale: Regulation 31(6)(c) lists the engine mount for cracks, looseness of mounting and looseness of the engine to the mount. Seat belts belong to the cabin group, tyres to the landing-gear group and wing fabric to the wing group.
